lead: nobody who works in that building has seen anything go wrong in nine years. you are in at five, on your own, and whatever the night did is finished and out of sight by the time the doors open.
sun: the covering gets built out of an hour. what failed at two in the morning is dealt with before anybody exists to see it — the part fetched off a man in the next county, the docket kept off the system — so the record is a line running normally at half seven. a hundred people work a full shift on top of a night that will never be mentioned to any of them.
moon: arriving is the whole of the trade, and the instinct came issued to be worked two-handed: a pair going out at speed, one driving while the other thinks. you have gone out on your own every time since you were twenty-six. so the thing standing over everybody's working week has one point of contact with the ground, and the point is a phone by a bed being answered.
pull: the fastest thing in you was built to go out in pairs. it has gone out alone for twenty years, and a whole site's clean record is standing on that.
tension: reliable gets said warmly, by people who would tell you the place would have shut a decade ago without you. the plant has been getting worse every year and no evidence of that exists anywhere, because clearing the evidence is what you have been doing since five o'clock every morning. so the case for spending on it cannot be put by anybody, including you, without opening nine years of mornings nobody was told about.
cost: an entire bad night can land in a business and leave nothing in it — no meeting, no customer told, nobody on that floor carrying a fortnight of worry they had no use for. the arrangement has one support and no second name on the rota. a week you cannot get in puts nine years into daylight at once, in one piece, with everyone standing in the middle of it.

lead: eleven of them are in your kitchen every year, and the family assembles because you assemble it. what keeps the evening warm is a thing you took in at nineteen and have not set down since.
sun: everybody in that family lives under a version of it that you put up. the aunt is difficult rather than cruel. the year he was away was work. all of that is true and all of it has had the worst part taken out before it reached the table. what got taken out went into you, and there is no provision anywhere in the arrangement for the one doing the taking out.
moon: a thing held has a morning at the end of it, when it goes to whoever it was always for, and the years only amount to anything because of that morning. yours sits inside a covering you built for the eleven of them, so the morning cannot be picked. and the whole assembly stands on one item, which is that you are the house they come to.
pull: you are holding the one thing that would explain all of them, and the only floor to set it down on is the floor they are standing on.
tension: your brother has been blaming the wrong person since he was twenty-two and has arranged his life around it — the visits he does not make, the way he says her name. one sentence from you ends that. the same sentence takes thirty years of an account away from six other people, none of whom asked to be protected and all of whom have been. so he stays wrong, and you stay the reason he can afford to be.
cost: two decades past the thing that should have finished that family, they are still a family and still warm, with nobody in it obliged to hold anything heavy. what you took in has aged past delivering. everyone it would have cleared is gone, the woman who said it is gone, and under the cover now there is a sentence with one witness and nowhere left to put it.

lead: she thinks she is the only one you do this for. so do the other five, and each of them is right about everything they can see, which is a payment that has arrived on the same day for years.
sun: money leaving you goes out under the same covering as everything else, which is why none of the six has ever been placed to work out that there are six. each arrangement got made privately, at a bad hour of somebody's life, with no version of it written down anywhere a person could come across it. from underneath, every one of them looks like generosity with room behind it.
moon: the six were not agreed by one person. whichever of you goes soft in a hospital corridor took two of them, the exact one took a third, and they have never sat down together to add anything up. you know the total to the pound, reached more than once at four in the morning, and it appears on no document, because putting it on paper means showing somebody the inside.
pull: six households are running on one income, each certain it is the only one, and the several of you who took them on have never once sat down and counted.
tension: everyone who has looked at your circumstances comes away with a figure out by a factor and no feeling of having been managed, because nothing is withheld except the six lines that decide it. an accountant asked once for the whole picture, got a warm partial one, and did not ask again. so the standing you have — solid, comfortable, obviously fine — is the thing that makes being close to the edge impossible to say out loud.
cost: six people got through the worst years they have had with the rent paid, no conditions attached, nobody else told, and nothing about it ever raised at a family thing afterwards. one income holds the lot, and an income does not sag first or give notice. a bad quarter and six households learn it on the same afternoon — about the money, and about each other.

lead: your father went through the whole of it between fifty and sixty-three and you were in the room for most of that. you are on the same road at a fixed distance behind, and nobody at home has been told.
sun: a body says nothing on its own, so the concealment costs you almost nothing. the management goes into ordinary hours — what comes off the plate, the hour the tablet goes in, the walk done before anybody is up — and every part of it passes for habit. so the household's week has never once been arranged around you, and what makes that possible is that nothing has been available to arrange it around.
moon: you have the whole course already, in order, from a distance of twenty-two years: which part arrives quickly, which one he concealed and for how long, what the third winter took off him. following a person never closes the gap, and this one has not moved in twenty-two years. so what sits under the cover is a dated schedule with his years written along it.
pull: you have already watched the whole of it happen once, at a distance of twenty-two years, and nobody in your house has been told which part of it you are in.
tension: a doctor asks what you eat and gets an accurate answer; nobody at home asks, because no occasion for it has ever come up. the household's account of you is a person of settled habits, and the habits are correct — the walk, the early hour, the thing declined at dinner — with the reason for each left out. what would land, said aloud, is the twenty-two years of already knowing, and it lands hardest on whoever watched him.
cost: your children remember a childhood with nothing wrong in it, and a decade has gone by without one evening of anybody's life spent on you. the whole covering stands on the current arrangement holding, and it will not thin out or lean first. the day it stops, they get the diagnosis and the twenty-two years of hiding it in one conversation, and the second is the part that gets discussed.
